subject: Energy
title: Grid Frequency: 50 Hz vs 60 Hz
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Grid Frequency: 50 Hz vs 60 Hz.

hook.text: AC grids run at a fixed frequency—60 Hz in the Americas and 50 Hz in most of Europe, Asia, and Africa.

buildup.text: Generators spin in sync at this frequency—all connected machines must rotate together, like a giant clock.

discovery.text: If frequency drops, demand exceeds supply—generators slow and stress builds. Rising frequency means oversupply.

twist.text: The UK once saw a frequency dip when millions turned on kettles during a TV commercial break—a 'TV pickup' surge.

climax.text: Grid operators watch frequency in real time—deploying reserves within seconds to keep it within ±0.5 Hz.

punchline.text: The grid's heartbeat is 50 or 60 Hz—skip a beat and trouble starts.

quiz.question: What does a drop in grid frequency indicate?
